headline: High: Authelia can forward auth decisions into Rasa channels, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes ForwardAuth and OAuth/OIDC flows, while Rasa ingests text/voice from chat channels. No shared filesystem or direct parser bridge is documented, so a prompt-injection path is not proven. The plausible bridge is manual or mediated content passing, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into Rasa training or runtime messages without sanitization
IF a shared chat or webhook channel forwards Authelia-generated text into Rasa as user-visible content
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between auth pages and bot prompts
Strip markup and control tokens before feeding auth text into Rasa
Use a human review step for any Authelia-generated message before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to forwarded messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic; Rasa processes text and voice over external messaging APIs. Even without a shared workspace, auth-related content can flow from Authelia into Rasa channels or logs in default integrations, creating a realistic leakage path with sensitive metadata exposure.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards identity or session metadata into a Rasa-connected channel
IF Rasa logs inbound messages containing auth tokens, identifiers, or account details
mitigations: Redact tokens and identifiers before any handoff to Rasa
Turn off verbose request logging on both systems
Restrict Rasa connectors to non-sensitive channels
Review outbound Authelia headers and claims before forwarding
requires-engineering: isolate auth and support data stores

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, and Rasa supports multiple external messaging APIs, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem writes or overlapping mutable resource ownership. The main conflict is limited to coordinated API-side effects, so the blast radius is smaller than a write-write collision.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external account or webhook endpoint
IF Authelia and Rasa are configured to mutate the same OAuth or messaging state
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts and API credentials
Disable concurrent writes to shared endpoints
Add a simple lock or queue around shared API mutations
Audit webhook destinations for overlap

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit auth decisions and claims, and Rasa can consume external messages and act as a support bot. If Rasa treats Authelia output as authoritative, an auth mistake or spoofed claim can cascade into incorrect support actions or user-facing responses. No verification step is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Authelia-generated claims as ground truth without verification
IF support workflows trigger actions based on auth status messages
mitigations: Require explicit verification before acting on auth claims
Label Authelia-derived fields as untrusted in Rasa
Add a confirmation step for any action based on auth state
Log and alert on mismatches between auth source and bot response

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and no PHI-specific or residency constraints are documented. Authelia handles authentication data and Rasa handles text/voice, so compliance risk is mainly policy mismatch in logging or retention rather than a clear residency breach. The lack of documented controls keeps this low, not none.
conditions: IF either system retains authentication transcripts longer than the other
IF support conversations include regulated identifiers and are stored in different jurisdictions
mitigations: Align retention settings across both systems
Minimize logged identity fields
Document data-class handling for auth and support traffic
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing
